title: Kernel selector v2: add registry entries for Mistral-family (L4/A10/A100/H100)
author: Grace Kim
description:
Motivation: Selector v2 is now table-driven via the kernel registry, but we only had "safe default" coverage for Mistral-family models. This PR adds tuned entries for Mistral-family across our main GPU SKUs and seq-length regimes (prefill vs decode; short vs long context buckets). Goal: reduce tail latency variance (especially A10 + long context) while preserving correctness by staying within the vetted kernel set.

Scope: Registry-only change + small validation/tests. No new kernels; no scheduler changes.

What changed (high level): Add Mistral-family rows to registry v1 with per-GPU selections for prefill/decode buckets; Add rationale annotations and links to benchmark-lab artifacts used to pick kernels; Extend registry validator tests to ensure we don’t accidentally create gaps (unknown bucket or GPU -> unsafe fallback) for Mistral-family.

Registry design notes: Model family key: mistral_family (covers Mistral-7B/Mixtral derivatives that share the same attention layout assumptions we currently detect, i.e., standard MHA/GQA variants already captured by the family mapping rules added in pr_18441); Buckets: prefill_short (<= 1k), prefill_long (> 1k), decode_short (<= 256 generated tokens), decode_long (> 256) — same bucket names used by selector v2 core; GPU keys: l4, a10, a100, h100 (normalized by SKU normalization layer).

Selected kernels (summary): L4: prefer "attn_flash_v3" for prefill_short + decode_short; use "attn_flash_v2_stable" for prefill_long to reduce p95 variance observed with v3 on long prompts; A10: force "attn_flash_v2_stable" for prefill_long + decode_long (mitigates the A10 long-context p95 regression we saw in earlier canary threads); A100: "attn_flash_v3" for all buckets; H100: "attn_flash_v3_sm90" for all buckets (keeps existing default).

Benchmark methodology + results: Benchmarks were run via benchmark-lab matrix (internal artifact: benchlab://selector-v2/2026-01-31/mistral-family-sweep) using representative prompt distributions (short chat, mixed, long context) and fixed batch sizing to isolate kernel effects. Reported deltas are v2 (with these entries) vs v2 (safe default entries), on the same runtime build.

Aggregate deltas (median across the prompt mix): L4: p95 latency -5.8% (prefill_long biggest win), tok/s +6.1%; A10: p95 latency -9.4% on long-context prompts, -1.2% overall; A100: p95 latency -3.0%, tok/s +2.7%; H100: within noise (<1%) but keeps consistent behavior.

Correctness: All selected kernels are within the conformance-tested kernel set. Re-ran conformance suite for Mistral-family shapes (see tests below).

Testing: CI unit tests (registry validator + selector unit tests); conformance-tests subset for Mistral-family: prefill/decode shapes across buckets (run: conformance://runs/2026-02-01/mistral-family-registry); benchmark-lab sanity run referenced above (not gating in CI).

Rollout impact: This only affects selector v2 traffic AND only for models mapped to mistral_family. If mapping fails or metadata is partial, selector falls back to safe kernel set (unchanged). No customer-facing config changes.

Follow-ups: If we see continued A10 decode_long variance at very high context lengths (>16k), we may need a narrower bucket or explicit override entry (tracked in ENG-3929 notes).

Checklist: [x] Registry entries include rationale + benchmark link; [x] Validator ensures no missing GPU/bucket keys; [x] Card. impact: no new label values; registry uses existing kernel IDs; [x] Conformance subset run attached.

Changed areas/files (representative): runtime/kernel_selector/registry/registry_v1.yaml; runtime/kernel_selector/registry/README.md; runtime/kernel_selector/registry/validator_test.cc; runtime/kernel_selector/selector_v2_registry_test.cc; tools/benchmarks/notes/mistral_family_kernel_sweep.md

Illustrative snippet (registry_v1.yaml):
- family: mistral_family bucket: prefill_long gpu: a10 kernel_id: attn_flash_v2_stable rationale: "A10 long-context p95 stabilization; see benchlab://selector-v2/2026-01-31/mistral-family-sweep"

Review notes: Hiro requested that we be conservative on A10 for long buckets; this PR sets A10 prefill_long + decode_long to v2_stable and adds a validator to prevent accidental regression if someone later edits just one bucket. Yuki asked to confirm SKU mapping (A10 vs A10G) doesn’t split the row; verified via normalization tests in pr_18463 and a quick local printout from the debug CLI.

Risk: Low/medium. Registry changes can still regress performance if wrong, but correctness risk is low because we are only picking kernels already in the conformance-tested set. Rollback is straightforward (registry revert or per-family override).
commits: Add validator coverage to prevent bucket/GPU gaps for Mistral-family
Document benchmark rationale and link artifacts
review_conversation: Hiro Tanaka: Can we avoid flash_v3 on A10 for long-context? We saw p95 spikes in the earlier sweep. Please bias stable unless the delta is clearly positive.
Grace Kim (author): Agreed. Updated A10 prefill_long + decode_long to attn_flash_v2_stable. Added a validator test to ensure we don’t accidentally mix stable/v3 across long buckets for this family.
Yuki Sato: Confirm the GPU key will match A10G instances too (we’ve had a few normalization misses). Also, can we add a note in the README on how to pick kernels for SM86 vs SM80?

Grace Kim (author): GPU normalization maps A10G -> a10 key in selector context; verified via local debug output + existing normalization tests. Added a short README note that registry keys are normalized SKUs and SM-specific selection lives in kernel_id variants (e.g., *_sm90).
Thomas Baird: Any telemetry/cardinality impact? New family value shows up in selector decision metrics; is that already bucketed/allowed?
Grace Kim (author): Family is already a controlled enum (and already emitted); adding mistral_family is expected and within the allowed set. No new high-cardinality labels added.
Noah Patel: Looks good. One nit: please keep rationale lines short so diffs stay readable; link to the sweep doc instead of embedding too much text.
Grace Kim (author): Done—trimmed rationale strings and moved details into tools/benchmarks/notes/mistral_family_kernel_sweep.md.
Rina Kobayashi: Bench artifact link is good; please also drop the prompt-mix config hash so we can reproduce exactly.
Grace Kim (author): Added prompt-mix config hash to the sweep notes.
